group.name: Buy (§8.5 #10)
group.string: The public log shows what is owed and what has been paid, so a shortfall can’t be hidden. It is still a promise, not a protocol rule.
The marketplace operator holds your payment until settlement.

The name is yours as soon as your payment is final. That part is protocol. The money is not: if this purchase loses a race or hits a cancelled sale, the operator refunds you. The public log shows what is owed and what has been paid, so a shortfall can’t be hidden. It is still a promise, not a protocol rule.
The marketplace operator holds payments and bids until settlement.

A name transfers on the chain the moment the payment is final. The money settles separately, through the operator: a purchase that loses a race or hits a cancelled sale is refunded, and so is a bid the moment it is outbid. The public log shows what is owed and what has been paid, so a shortfall can’t be hidden. It is still a promise, not a protocol rule.
You get {netNim} NIM if it sells, after the {percent} marketplace commission.
You get at least {minNetNim} NIM, after the {percent} commission on the winning bid.

group.string: Names and prices here are for testing.

This is a test era. Every clock runs short so a name's whole life fits a few days: a term is 1 year instead of a year, a lifetime about 100 years instead of 100 years, and prices are set for testing. Nothing registered here carries over. The registry starts again at launch.

group.name: Before LAUNCH_HEIGHT
group.string: The registry opens Thursday, January 1, around 01:00 AM GMT+1.

Nimiq Names starts at block 62,275,680. Nothing sent before that block is read, so a registration sent early registers nothing. The time shown is an estimate from the chain's height; this notice disappears when the block arrives.
